description: Robo directs a movie: the script's words spill into a pile, and Bear, Penguin and Frog sort naming words (person, animal, place, thing) into a blue basket and doing words into a red one, see the difference with the Freeze Camera, then join one of each into sentences.

youtube.title: Nouns and Verbs for Kids! Naming Words and Doing Words | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Lights, camera... action! Robo's movie script has spilled into a messy pile, and Bear, Penguin and Frog don't know what to do. Kids sort naming words (nouns: a person, an animal, a place or a thing) into the blue basket and doing words (verbs: jump, clap, slide, swim) into the red basket. The Freeze Camera shows the difference: when we freeze, the bear is still there, but the clapping stops. Then one naming word plus one doing word makes a sentence: The bear claps.

For first graders (CCSS L.1.1.b, L.1.1.e).

Try at home: with a grown-up, write naming words on blue paper and doing words on red paper. Act out a red card, then freeze! Make a sentence with one blue card and one red card. Act in a clear space with soft landings.

do.text: Let me check the script. Oh no!
All the words fell out in a messy pile.
Our movie needs two kinds of words.
Words that name who is in it...
...and words that say what they do!
A clapperboard helps film makers match sound and picture.
A naming word names someone or something.
Me! A frog is an animal!
So frog is a naming word. Blue basket!
Bear! That names me. I'm an animal.
Teacher. A person who helps us learn.
Baker. A person who bakes yummy treats.
Friend. A person who plays with you.
Pond. A place where frogs swim.
House. A place where you live.
Park. A place with benches and swings.
Naming words name a person, animal, place or thing.
Grown-ups call a naming word a noun.
A doing word tells what someone does.
Can you do it? Show me!
Bears stand up tall to see and smell better!
Penguins slide on their bellies. It's called tobogganing!
Swim! Swim your arms like this.
Read! I hold my book like this.
Sleep! Rest your head on your hands.
Jump goes in... the blue basket!
No, Robo! Jump is something you do!
Oops! Jump is a doing word. Red basket!
Grown-ups call a doing word a verb.
This is my Freeze Camera. Action, everyone!
Freeze! The bear is still here. The penguin is still here.
Bear, penguin, frog: naming words stay.
But the clapping and sliding stopped.
Clap and slide: doing words stop when we freeze.
Wait. Frog, your toe is tapping!
I can't help it! My toes love doing words!
Freeze game! Move like Frog, then freeze!
Did you stay still? Great freezing!
One blue naming card, plus one red doing card.
Shh! Now swap the naming word!
A sentence needs both: who, and what they do.
Name it, do it, that's a sentence!
Quiz time! Blue basket or red basket?
Blue! Pond is a place. A naming word!
Red! Swim is something I do.
Question three. The bear claps. Which is the doing word?
Question four. Which is a naming word: hat or hop?
Hat! A hat is a thing. Hop is a doing word.
Last one. Say a doing word for Penguin!
Slides! Swims! Waddles! Flaps! They're all right!
I did it! Freeze is a doing word too!
Naming words name a person, animal, place or thing.
Doing words tell what they do. Together, a sentence!
